Pipe and fittings will be selected to minimize differences in wall thicknesses. Where necessary, transitions between differing wall thicknesses are made in accordance with ASME B31.4 guidelines. Transitions at weld connections between pipe and fittings of unequal wall thickness will be made in accordance with Figure 434.8.6‐2 of ASME B31.4. All first connections to the pipeline shall be welded. The second connection, if equal to or greater than 2‐inch, shall be raised face. All materials shall conform to the applicable API, ASTM, MSS or ASME minimum requirements. Where possible, all standard pipe and manifold fittings will be selected to match pipe wall thickness and grade. All fittings will be manufactured in accordance with the applicable specification(s) in Table 6-2. Table 6-2Fittings and Flanges Specification SPECIFICATION DESCRIPTION ASME B16.5 Pipe Flanges and Flanged Fittings ASME B16.9 Factory‐Made Wrought Buttwelding Fittings ASME B16.25 Butt‐welding Ends ASME B16.47 Large Diameter Steel Flanges MSS‐SP‐44 Steel Pipeline Flanges MSS‐SP‐75 High Strength, Wrought, Butt Welding Fittings 6.3.3 Bolts, Nuts and Gaskets Bolts and studs shall comply with ASTM A320 Grade L7; nuts shall meet ASTM A194 / A194M Grade 7 Heavy Hex specifications. All bolts or studs shall extend completely through their nuts and have full thread engagement. A minimum two‐thread protrusion is required. For corrosion resistance studs and nuts will be PTFE coated when specified. Gaskets shall be spiral would type with stainless steel winding, non‐asbestos filler material and include an internal ring to prevent unwinding of the gasket. Flexitallic CGI, or equal is acceptable. 6.3.4 In-Line Inspection Accommodation Note that the proposed pipelines will be designed and installed with provision for internal pipeline inspection. Page 12 of 20 Design Basis Memorandum 1997-000-PL-DBM-0001 Revision: 0 Pipeline Scope - FEED Date: April 28, 2023 The pipeline will be inspected after the hydrostatic test using an ILI Caliper tool to identify possible manufacturing or construction‐related issues (including ovality, external gouges, dents, and buckles). The required acceptance criteria will be: • No more than 2% deviation of the inside diameter of the pipe (from dents or buckles with metal loss) • No more than 5% deviation on pipe ovality (from cold bends and overburden) Barred tees (scraper bars) shall be installed along all mainline branch connections which are greater than or equal to half the size of the line pipe, to facilitate pigging. Facility and pipeline design will account for size and workspace requirements for pigging activities. Intelligent tools planned for use in this system will be defined during the Detailed Design phase and this section updated with criteria for pipeline design required to support safe and effective tool runs. 6.4 BENDING 6.4.1 Field Bends Cold bends are to be field fabricated in accordance with the provisions outlined in 49 CFR, Part 195, ASME B31.4, and Project Specification.
